Zenoh key-space prefixes were extracted with a single grep pattern for double-quoted 'root/seg1/seg2' literals; single-quoted keys, string-concatenated keys (e.g. Gleam <> or OCaml ^ built subjects), and keys built at runtime from variables are not captured, so the indrajaal/c3i/uos prefix lists are a lower bound, not exhaustive.

The coordination events schema (uos-session-sync/v1) overloads the 'a' field per-operation (provider at register, task ref at claim, 'broadcast' at send, a nonce at heartbeat, a bookmark name at release); 'provider from the newest event per session' was resolved two ways (register-derived and literal-newest) because the literal reading is not always a real provider name.

Clock-skew observation (not a B13 gap per se): host `date -u` reported 2026-09-07T15:19Z while some already-written document filenames in this same workspace carry later prefixes (e.g. 20260907-1533-...) written by concurrent swarm workers; this looks like ordinary multi-agent write-ahead-of-read timing during a live swarm run rather than a clock fault, but was not independently verified against chrony/timesync receipts as SC-TIME would require.

'20 most recent by timestamp prefix' could not be computed meaningfully for the 'component' or 'artifact' kinds because component source files carry no timestamp prefix and this jj workspace checkout stamps every file with an identical mtime at workspace creation, so a genuine last-touched ordering is not recoverable from the filesystem alone; the document kind's 20-most-recent list (which does have timestamp-prefixed filenames) was computed instead and stands in for that requirement.
